domain: EU public procurement / tender competition prediction
prediction_question: At the TED publication of a contract notice (call for competition), will the linked award notice report that the procedure's lot received exactly one offer (single bid)?
prediction_time: The TED publication instant of the contract notice (CN). The CN CSV export carries the buyer's dispatch date (DT_DISPATCH) and year; the exact publication date (PD) per notice is served by the anonymous TED Search API v3. Worked example in notes.md: CN 10-2023 dispatched 2022-12-28, published 2023-01-02+01:00 (Europe/Brussels); its linked award notice 371295-2023 was published 2023-06-21+02:00, i.e. the whole target window (award decision, offers received) follows the prediction instant.
target_definition: Binary single-bid label per procedure lot: NUMBER_OFFERS = 1 in the linked contract award notice (CAN) row for that lot, vs NUMBER_OFFERS > 1. Label source columns: CAN's NUMBER_OFFERS (plus the FUTURE_CAN_ID join key); both excluded from any shipped features. Pre-eForms CANs also carry NUMBER_TENDERS_SME / NUMBER_TENDERS_OTHER_EU / NUMBER_TENDERS_NON_EU breakdowns of the same total.

sources.name: TED CSV subset - Tenders Electronic Daily public procurement notices (contract notices 2006-2023, contract award notices 2007-2023), data.europa.eu dataset ted-csv

sources.access: anonymous direct download; CN export carries FUTURE_CAN_ID / FUTURE_CAN_ID_ESTIMATED - the Publications Office's own pre-computed CN->CAN link; measured populated 10/10 complete rows in the CN 2019 prefix and present in first CN 2023 rows; link fixtures verified against the Search API (notes.md)
sources.licence: Commission Decision 2011/833/EU per the TED legal notice copyright section (read 2026-10-27): procurement notices freely reusable for commercial and non-commercial purposes with attribution; class B

data.europa.eu catalogue records ted-1 / ted-csv (read 2026-10-27): access_right PUBLIC, publisher 'Publications Office of the European Union'; distribution-level licence fields are null, so the publisher's legal notice and Commission Decision 2011/833/EU are the operative instruments; the ted-csv description notes eForms became the additional standard on 14 November 2022 and EC GROW (GROW-D2@ec.europa.eu) welcomes links to reuse research.
split_strategy: Not built - the mirror veto precedes construction. Measured anchors any future reformulation would build on: award-notice population by era (Search API totalNoticeCount, 2026-10-27): FT=3 (legacy award form) 38,898 in June 2019 alone; FT="CAN" (eForms result notices) 0 in June 2015, 1,147 in June 2019, 723 in June 2022, 1,161 in June 2023, full-year 2023 34,699, 28,676 in June 2024, 33,463 in June 2025, 35,853 in September 2026. CSV prefix samples (first ~256 KiB per year file, early-January notices, NOT year-representative): NUMBER_OFFERS populated on 64.4% of rows (2019), 58.2% (2021), 72.3% (2023); single-bid share among populated rows 32.7% / 31.8% / 42.8%. Full-population eligible counts (CANs with offers populated AND linked CN) require bulk processing on a worker - recorded as a prerequisite, not measured here.

measurements.bulk_inventory_2026_10_27: data.europa.eu ted-csv catalogue: annual CN zips 2006-2023 and CAN zips 2007-2023 plus combined packages and a deprecated V1/V2.2 line; last catalogue update 2024-01-25; no 2024+ CSV distribution, so the CSV subset ends at 2023 while the Search API continues (measured 35,853 eForms CANs in Sept 2026). CAN 2023 zip = 111,181,340 bytes; CN 2023 zip = 42,882,577 bytes (Content-Range totals via ranged GET; HEAD returns 401).
measurements.can_csv_schema_2026_10_27: 74 columns incl. ID_NOTICE_CAN, DT_DISPATCH, CORRECTIONS, CAE_NAME/CAE_NATIONALID/CAE_TOWN, ISO_COUNTRY_CODE, CAE_TYPE, MAIN_ACTIVITY, TYPE_OF_CONTRACT (S/U/W), TAL_LOCATION_NUTS, CPV, ID_LOT, LOTS_NUMBER, VALUE_EURO, TOP_TYPE (procedure), B_ACCELERATED, CRIT_CODE/CRIT_PRICE_WEIGHT, B_ELECTRONIC_AUCTION, NUMBER_AWARDS, ID_AWARD, INFO_ON_NON_AWARD, B_CONTRACTOR_SME, TITLE, NUMBER_OFFERS, NUMBER_TENDERS_SME, NUMBER_TENDERS_OTHER_EU, NUMBER_TENDERS_NON_EU, NUMBER_OFFERS_ELECTR, AWARD_EST_VALUE_EURO, AWARD_VALUE_EURO, DT_AWARD. Header + leading rows recovered by a ranged 256 KiB read + partial inflate (262,144 bytes -> ~1.5 MB CSV, ~2,361 rows for 2023), recorded in probe/probe_csv_prefix.py.
measurements.cn_csv_schema_2026_10_27: 64 columns incl. ID_NOTICE_CN, DT_DISPATCH, FUTURE_CAN_ID, FUTURE_CAN_ID_ESTIMATED, buyer fields, TYPE_OF_CONTRACT, TAL_LOCATION_NUTS, CPV, ID_LOT, LOTS_NUMBER, B_VARIANTS, VALUE_EURO (estimated), B_OPTIONS, DURATION, CONTRACT_START/CONTRACT_COMPLETION, TOP_TYPE, B_ACCELERATED, ENV_OPERATORS/MIN/MAX, CRIT_CODE/CRIT_PRICE_WEIGHT, DT_APPLICATIONS (deadline), B_RECURRENT_PROCUREMENT.
measurements.link_verification_2026_10_27: FUTURE_CAN_ID populated in 10/10 complete rows of the CN 2019 prefix (all ESTIMATED=0) and in the first CN 2023 rows. Two fixtures verified against the Search API: CN 10-2023 (PRT, Instituto Superior Tecnico, CPV 90910000, dispatched 2022-12-28, published 2023-01-02+01:00) -> FUTURE_CAN_ID 371295-2023, which the API returns as a CAN published 2023-06-21+02:00, CY=PRT, matching authority code; CN 2-2023 (ESP, Consejeria de Presidencia, dispatched 2022-12-28) -> 181795-2023, a CAN published 2023-03-27+02:00, CY=ESP. Both targets follow the prediction instant by months. Recorded in probe/probe_api_counts.py.
measurements.form_type_vocabulary_2026_10_27: The expert query FT field distinguishes legacy standard-form families (FT=3 = award notices under the classic directives; 38,898 in June 2019) from eForms result notices (FT="CAN"; 0 in June 2015 before eForms existed, 640 in January 2023 during the transition, 28,676-35,853 per month by 2024-2026). A full award population needs both families plus the other legacy award form codes; the CSV subset aggregates all families, which is why construction should count from the CSV/API pair rather than FT="CAN" alone.
measurements.baserate_prefix_samples_2026_10_27: CAN CSV year-file prefixes (first ~256 KiB compressed, ordered by notice ID = early-January notices; explicitly NOT year-representative): 2019: 3,343 rows / 706 notices, NUMBER_OFFERS populated 64.4%, single-bid 704 (32.7% of populated), multi 1,450, zero 0, INFO_ON_NON_AWARD set 9.5%; 2021: 4,049 rows / 568 notices, populated 58.2%, single 749 (31.8%); 2023: 2,361 rows / 722 notices, populated 72.3%, single 731 (42.8%). These match the ~30-40% single-bidding phenomenon published by the European Court of Auditors (SR 28/2023) and the Commission's Single Market Scoreboard, which is the cross-check against the publisher's own summary product.
measurements.fetch_cost_measured_2026_10_27: ranged 256 KiB zip-prefix fetch 0.29-0.33 s each (three years measured); Search API count query 0.08-0.16 s; search response with converted full-text content ~5-10 KB per notice (multilingual). Full construction would download ~150 MiB compressed per CN+CAN year pair on a worker (~1.5 GiB for 2014-2023), well inside worker norms and far above coordinator limits - bulk stays on workers.
measurements.novelty_prior_art_2026_10_27: The exact task exists in reproducible form: Acikalin, Gorgun, Kutlu & Tas, 'How you describe procurement calls matters: Predicting outcome of public procurement using call descriptions', Natural Language Engineering 30(6) 2024 (online 2023-08-10): four prediction tasks on THIS TED CSV subset (number of offers PNumOffers; single offer PSingleOffer; foreign-firm award; price overrun vs estimate), 333,832 notices, 80/20 train/test, scored transformers, and released code: github.com/utkuumur/HowYouDescribeProcurementCallsMatters. Adjacent prior art: Demiray, Ozbayoglu & Tas 2015 (bidder counts on TED); Gallego, Rivero & Martinez 2021; 'Intensifying Competition in Public Procurement' (Springer GIQ 2023, TED 2017-2020 offers modelling); ECA Special Report 28/2023 single-bidding dashboard (DG GROW TED CSV + DigiWhist opentender); MDPI Algorithms 2025 (SME winner + main activity, TED 2015-2023); Spanish bidder-recommender (Wiley 2020). ML-ready data compilations already public: PleIAs/TEDEUTenders (HF parquet by year), EUROPROCURE-10 (HF, 2016-2025), zalizedata TED+OCDS (HF/Kaggle, 6.3M notices - NC licensed, unusable for us, but demonstrates availability).

rejection_reason: Mirror with the precedent named. The task this source most naturally carries - predicting single bids / number of offers at call-for-competition publication on the TED CSV subset - already exists as a published, scored prediction study with released construction code (Acikalin et al., Natural Language Engineering 2024, tasks PSingleOffer/PNumOffers; github.com/utkuumur/HowYouDescribeProcurementCallsMatters), on the same data, same prediction instant, same population, with train/test splits and reported results. What we would add (temporal splits instead of random, structured CN features plus text, the official FUTURE_CAN_ID link, our qualification gate and published artifact) is engineering refinement of an existing task, not genuinely novel work; the operator's standing bar is to ship nothing rather than mirror. Related targets on this source are also taken: foreign-firm award and price overrun (NLE 2024), SME-winner and buyer main-activity (MDPI Algorithms 2025), winner/bidder recommendation (Wiley 2020), single-bidding rates as policy indicator (ECA SR 28/2023).
review: The licence is clean (class B: Commission Decision 2011/833/EU reuse, attribution, no distortion, personal-data caveat handled by excluding contact-person fields), the access is unusually good for this bench (official annual CSV extracts plus an anonymous search API), and the official CN->CAN link column (FUTURE_CAN_ID) removes the main construction risk - which is precisely why the source is heavily mined. Both timing and target contracts are satisfiable, so this is not a weak-source rejection; it is a strong source whose obvious task is taken. Recorded so no future tick re-probes TED blind, and so the measured access map (CSV subset ends 2023; FT vocabulary split legacy/eForms; link fixtures) is reusable for any genuinely different formulation.
next_action: Closed for any target that is a bucket of the number of offers received (incl. zero-offer / no-award / INFO_ON_NON_AWARD variants, which are thresholds of PNumOffers) and for foreign-winner, SME-winner, price-overrun, main-activity and bidder-recommendation targets - all covered by the named prior art. Reopen only with a task contract whose target is a different variable measured in this data product AND its own recorded novelty sweep that clears the mirror rule; the as-of/vintage question (CSV subset is a year-end export; corrections are separate notices) would then also need explicit as-of evidence per the prediction contract. Reusable measured facts are in measurements and probe/.
